full_judgment: 13. The cardinal principles of criminal jurisprudence are the presumption of innocence of the accused and burden of proving the guilty of the accused is always on the prosecution. This fundamental principles has been incorporated in our substantive and procedural criminal laws. The burden of proof in criminal law signifies that the prosecution must establish the charge against the accused beyond all reasonable doubt and if there is any doubt the benefit must go to the accused person.
